name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3336: The second eye read v3334 and found its git rule fragile in the DANGEROUS direction. That cut located the git subcommand by stepping over global flags, consuming one extra token for each flag in a known list. MEASURED 2 of 6 wrong, both FALSE NEGATIVES: a git-dir path containing a SPACE splits into pieces so the scan landed on the fragment and read the subcommand as spaces, and an unlisted value-taking flag put its own VALUE there and read the subcommand as that. Either one hides a real git push, and a hidden push is a version banked into a tree a gate is grading. THE LIST OF VALUE-TAKING FLAGS CAN NEVER BE COMPLETE. The list of subcommands that legitimately take push as an ARGUMENT can be, and is small and stable: branch, checkout, log, tag, config, remote and their kin. So the scan now walks the tokens and stops at whichever comes FIRST, push or one of those, and an unrecognised bare token, which is exactly what a flag value or an unknown subcommand looks like, simply keeps scanning. It fails toward TRUE on the unknown, because a missed push banks a bad version while a spurious refusal costs one re-run. Re-measured across 25 cases: 0 wrong. Both eye findings now pass, every earlier negative still refuses including git config push.default and a remote named push, and a free tree still answers free. 5 red-proofs PROVEN. One was REMOVED as superseded, its anchor being the flag-stepping line this cut replaced.
